label: rem:pairing-gauge-fluctuation-massless-interpretation
title: Interpretation: pairing fluctuations as a graviton candidate
html:
Interpretive remark (physical reading; not part of the mathematical claim).

If the Frobenius pairing is read as a metric, a fluctuation \delta\lambda of the pairing is the categorical analogue of a metric perturbation h_{\mu\nu}. Under that reading, the proposition is the algebraic shadow of the familiar statement of linearised gravity that pure-gauge perturbations h \mapsto h + \mathcal{L}_\xi \bar g cost no action: the infinitesimal automorphism f plays the role of the vector field \xi, the combination f \otimes \mathrm{id} - \mathrm{id} \otimes f^{\vee} that of the Lie derivative of the background, and the vanishing of S(\delta_f\lambda) together with the radical condition is what "no mass term along gauge directions" means for a quadratic action.

This gives one precise candidate content for the sentence in the mass endomorphism conjecture that "the graviton is the residual of \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} after subtracting the Higgs contribution": the graviton is read as a pairing fluctuation, and the proposition shows that its gauge part carries no mass term for the contraction action. What is not shown, and would be needed before the reading could be called a derivation:

  1. that the gauge directions exhaust the zero modes of a non-degenerate pairing action (the contraction action has rank at most one, as the proposition notes, so it cannot decide this);
  2. that the physical (non-gauge) fluctuations transform as a spin-2 isotypic piece, i.e. the symmetric traceless part of \mathrm{Sym}^2 of a spin-1 object;
  3. any relation between the contraction action and \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} itself;
  4. that the ambient category carries a braiding, which the proposition needs in order to apply to the co-pairing that the Frobenius pairing itself supplies.

No physical constant, dimension or signature enters the proposition or this reading.
